name: Shell-Only vs Turnkey Commercial Construction Costs in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What is the realistic per-square-foot cost range for shell-only versus turnkey commercial build-outs in Los Angeles County in the current market?
mainEntity.text: What is the realistic per-square-foot cost range for shell-only versus turnkey commercial build-outs in Los Angeles County in the current market?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Los Angeles County, many published cost guides give broad commercial cost ranges, but they rarely separate shell-only from turnkey, tenant-ready projects in a way owners can use. In practice, you need three separate ranges: shell building, core MEP systems, and interior build-out. A basic shell for a low- to mid-rise commercial structure with minimal architectural complexity will typically sit at the low to mid end of published regional ranges because it excludes interior partitions, finishes, and specialty systems. As soon as you add full HVAC distribution, electrical distribution, restrooms, elevators (for multi-story), fire sprinklers, and code-required accessibility features, the cost per square foot increases noticeably. Turnkey spaces—offices, medical suites, restaurants, and retail—stack interior build-out on top of shell and systems. These include partitions, doors, casework, ceilings, lighting, flooring, specialty mechanical or plumbing (for example, for kitchens or medical gas), and higher-end finishes. Tenant improvement allowances rarely cover all of this in Los Angeles’ current market, especially for complex uses. The best way to budget is to ask your contractor or estimator to give you separate line-item per-square-foot allowances for shell, building systems, and build-out by use type and finish quality rather than relying on a single blended number that hides large cost components.
acceptedAnswer.description: Per-square-foot commercial construction costs in Los Angeles County differ sharply between shell-only and turnkey projects. Shell buildings for low-rise commercial can be significantly cheaper than fully finished, tenant-ready spaces that include MEP systems, interiors, and upgrades. Owners should budget separate ranges for shell, core systems, and interior build-out based on use and finish level.
